raw_response:
I've been working this land for 30 years in Quzhou. I know what the soil wants and what the market looks like from experience. Let me think through this.

My 5 mu breaks down the way it always has — 3 mu in cotton, which is my main cash crop and what this county does best. The other 2 mu I run in the wheat-maize rotation: winter wheat goes in after October, maize follows right after the wheat harvest in June. Same 2 mu, different seasons. That rotation keeps my household fed and gives me a bit of extra grain to sell.

Cotton is labor-heavy, especially at picking time. With just two of us at home now and one working some off-farm jobs, I can't push more than 3 mu of cotton or I'll be overwhelmed come September. Bt hybrid seed costs more but cuts down my pesticide runs — worth it. I'll plough deep before planting cotton, like I always do, gets the roots down. For wheat I'll use rotary tillage, and I'll go no-till on the maize right into the wheat stubble. Saves me time and diesel.

My well is reliable, so irrigation isn't a worry. I'll do 5 waterings on the cotton — pre-plant, bud stage, flowering, boll-setting, and one late one if it's dry. Wheat gets 3: base, jointing, heading. Maize gets 3: emergence, tasseling, grain fill.

I'll apply fertilizer the same way I have for years. Maybe slightly more nitrogen on cotton this year since I heard soil tests in the area show depletion. I won't overdo it — waste of money.
